problems.title: Unique Paths
problems.statement: Robot at (0,0) in m x n grid wants to move to (m-1, n-1). Can only move down or right. Return total unique paths.
problems.understanding: To reach cell (r, c), you can arrive from top (r-1, c) or left (r, c-1). Thus dp[r][c] = dp[r-1][c] + dp[r][c-1].

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: At every cell, recursively branch right and down until reaching bottom-right corner.

problems.intuition: Fill 2D grid bottom-up or optimize space to 1D row array of size n.
problems.approach:
1. Initialize dp = [1] * n.
  2. Loop m-1 times: for c from 1 to n-1, dp[c] += dp[c-1].
  3. Return dp[-1].
problems.takeaway: Grid DP — Each cell transitions from top and left adjacent neighbors.

problems.title: Longest Common Subsequence
problems.statement: Given two strings text1 and text2, return length of their longest common subsequence.
problems.understanding: At each pair of characters: if equal → take both (1 + dfs(i+1, j+1)). Otherwise → skip one side (max(dfs(i+1, j), dfs(i, j+1))).

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: Recursively match characters or branch by skipping one side.

problems.intuition: 2D DP matrix dp[i][j] where i and j index text1 and text2. Space can be optimized to 1D row array.
problems.approach:
1. Create dp grid of size (m+1) x (n+1).
  2. Loop i from 1 to m and j from 1 to n.
  3. If text1[i-1] == text2[j-1]: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1. Else dp[i][j] = max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).
  4. Return dp[m][n].

optimal.title: Optimized Code (Python 3)
complexity: Space: O(min(m,n)) (Space Optimized) / O(mn) (2D DP Matrix)

problems.takeaway: Two-String DP — Compare prefix i of string A and prefix j of string B.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy & Sell Stock with Cooldown
problems.statement: Find max profit trading stock. After selling a stock, you cannot buy stock on the next day (cooldown 1 day).
problems.understanding: States: BUY (can buy or skip), SELL (can sell -> forces day i+2 cooldown), COOLDOWN.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: Branch recursively between buy, sell, and cooldown choices.

problems.approach:
1. Initialize hold = -prices[0], sold = 0, cooldown = 0.
  2. For price in prices[1:]: update state variables according to transitions.
  3. Return max(sold, cooldown).
problems.takeaway: State Machine DP — Model transitions between BUY, SELL, and COOLDOWN explicitly.

problems.title: Coin Change II
problems.statement: Count the number of combinations to make an amount using given coin denominations (unlimited supply).
problems.understanding: Unbounded Knapsack combinations! Outer loop must iterate coins first to avoid counting permutations twice (e.g. 1+2 vs 2+1).

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: Try taking or skipping each coin recursively.

problems.intuition: dp[c] += dp[c - coin]. Outer loop iterating coins ensures ordering is fixed and combinations are counted.
problems.approach:
1. Initialize dp = [0] * (amount + 1) and dp[0] = 1.
  2. For coin in coins: for current from coin to amount: dp[current] += dp[current - coin].
  3. Return dp[amount].
problems.takeaway: Unbounded Knapsack Combinations — Outer loop over coins, inner loop increasing order over amount.

problems.title: Target Sum
problems.statement: Assign + or - to every number in nums to reach target. Return total ways.
problems.understanding: Can be converted to a subset sum problem: P - N = target and P + N = total ⇒ P = (total + target) // 2.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: Try adding and subtracting each number recursively.

problems.intuition: Reduce problem to finding subset sum equal to (total + target) // 2 using 0/1 Knapsack 1D DP.
problems.approach:
1. Compute total = sum(nums). If abs(target) > total or (total + target) % 2, return 0.
  2. subset = (total + target) // 2.
  3. Initialize dp = [0] * (subset + 1) with dp[0] = 1.
  4. For num in nums: loop current backward from subset down to num: dp[current] += dp[current - num]. Return dp[subset].
problems.takeaway: Subset Sum Reduction — Transform +/- Target Sum into 0/1 Knapsack subset counting.

problems.title: Interleaving String
problems.statement: Determine whether s3 can be formed by interleaving s1 and s2.
problems.understanding: If len(s1) + len(s2) != len(s3) return False. dp[i][j] tracks whether s1[:i] and s2[:j] interleave to form s3[:i+j].

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: Branch recursively whenever current char of s1 or s2 matches s3.

problems.intuition: 2D boolean table dp[i][j] where dp[i][j] = (dp[i-1][j] and s1[i-1] == s3[k]) or (dp[i][j-1] and s2[j-1] == s3[k]).
problems.approach:
1. Check length validity: if len(s1) + len(s2) != len(s3) return False.
  2. Create grid dp of size (m+1) x (n+1) with dp[0][0] = True.
  3. Fill table row by row from 0 to m and column from 0 to n.
  4. Return dp[m][n].
problems.takeaway: Two-String Grid DP — Path matching in a 2D matrix representing positions in s1 and s2.

problems.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
problems.statement: Given an m x n integers matrix, return the length of the longest increasing path in matrix.
problems.understanding: Since paths must be strictly increasing, there are no cycles (DAG). DFS + Memoization is natural DP on DAG.
problems.intuition: Memoize memo[r][c] storing longest increasing path starting at cell (r, c).
problems.approach:
1. Initialize memo grid with 0s.
  2. In dfs(r, c): if memo[r][c] already computed, return it.
  3. Explore 4 orthogonal directions where matrix[nr][nc] > matrix[r][c], update best = max(best, 1 + dfs(nr, nc)).
  4. Store memo[r][c] = best and return. Max over all cells is the result.

problems.title: Distinct Subsequences
problems.statement: Count how many times t occurs as a subsequence of s.
problems.understanding: At matching character s[i-1] == t[j-1], we can use it (dp[i-1][j-1]) or skip it (dp[i-1][j]). Sum both choices!

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: At every matching character, recursively try using it or skipping it.

problems.intuition: 2D DP table dp[i][j] storing ways to form t[:j] using prefix s[:i].
problems.approach:
1. Initialize dp = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(m + 1)].
  2. Base case: dp[i][0] = 1 for all i (empty string t is always 1 subsequence).
  3. For i from 1 to m and j from 1 to n: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j]. If s[i-1] == t[j-1], dp[i][j] += dp[i-1][j-1].
  4. Return dp[m][n].
problems.takeaway: Two-String Counting DP — Sum choice paths when characters match.

problems.title: Edit Distance
problems.statement: Given strings word1 and word2, return minimum operations (insert, delete, replace) to convert word1 to word2.
problems.understanding: Standard Levenshtein distance 2D DP. 3 operations at each position: Insert, Delete, or Replace.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: Recursive evaluation trying all 3 operations (insert, delete, replace) at each step.

problems.intuition: 2D bottom-up grid dp[i][j] where dp[i][j] is min operations for word1[:i] and word2[:j]. Can be space-optimized to 1D row array of size min(m, n).
problems.approach:
1. Initialize 2D array dp of size (m+1) x (n+1) with base cases dp[i][0] = i and dp[0][j] = j.
  2. For i from 1 to m and j from 1 to n: if word1[i-1] == word2[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1].
  3. Else dp[i][j] = 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]) (delete, insert, replace).
  4. Return dp[m][n].
problems.takeaway: Insert / Delete / Replace Two-String DP — Standard edit distance pattern comparing character prefixes.

problems.title: Burst Balloons
problems.statement: Burst balloon i to gain nums[i-1] * nums[i] * nums[i+1] coins. Return max total coins.
problems.understanding: Instead of choosing the first balloon to burst, choose the LAST balloon to burst in an interval (left, right)!

naive.title: Naive Solution — Recursion
naive.html: Try every balloon as the first balloon to burst recursively.

problems.intuition: Pad array with 1 at both ends: nums = [1] + nums + [1]. Evaluate interval lengths from 2 to n. Choose balloon k burst last in (left, right).
problems.approach:
1. Pad array with boundary 1s: nums = [1] + nums + [1].
  2. Create 2D DP matrix dp of size n x n.
  3. Outer loop length from 2 to n-1; inner loop left from 0 to n - length; right = left + length.
  4. Loop k from left + 1 to right - 1: coins = nums[left] * nums[k] * nums[right]. Update dp[left][right] = max(dp[left][right], dp[left][k] + coins + dp[k][right]).
  5. Return dp[0][n - 1].
problems.takeaway: Interval DP → choose the last operation inside an interval. This is one of the most important advanced DP patterns.

problems.title: Regular Expression Matching
problems.statement: Given input string s and pattern p, implement regex matching with '.' (matches any single char) and '*' (matches zero or more of preceding element).
problems.understanding: Recursive branching occurs whenever * appears in pattern. State is represented by pair of indices (i, j) for s and p.
problems.intuition: Cache recursive subproblems with hash table memo[(i, j)] storing boolean results for matching s[i:] and p[j:].
problems.approach:
1. Initialize memo = {}.
  2. In dfs(i, j): check if (i, j) in memo. If j == len(p) return i == len(s).
  3. Check first_match = i < len(s) and (p[j] == s[i] or p[j] == '.').
  4. If j + 1 < len(p) and p[j+1] == '*': set answer = dfs(i, j+2) or (first_match and dfs(i+1, j)).
  5. Else: set answer = first_match and dfs(i+1, j+1).
  6. Store memo[(i, j)] = answer and return.
problems.takeaway: 2D State DP / DFS + Memoization — Handles wildcard matching by memoizing (i, j) states across recursive branches.
